items.e: AND THE LORD SPOKE. It is truly not proper for an intelligent person to scrutinize God’s actions and ask, why did the Lord act thus? For all of God’s actions are done wisely. Man’s wisdom is as nothing before God. I mention this because you will read in this Torah portion that God guilefully commanded the Israelites to turn back so that Pharaoh would go out and pursue them, and drown in the sea. God’s thoughts are very deep.
PI-HAHIROTH. Pi-hahiroth is elsewhere called Pene-hahiroth (Num. 33:8). It is so called because the mouth ( peh ) is on the face ( panim ). It is the name of a place.

BEFORE BAAL-ZEPHON. Some say that the Egyptian magicians made bronze images which drew power from the stars, and that Baal-zephon was a statue that no slave fleeing Egypt was able to pass by. It is because of this that Scripture reads, that the people were fled (v. 5). However, in my opinion because Moses said to Pharaoh, We will go three days’ journey into the wilderness (Ex. 8:23), it appeared to Pharaoh from these words that Moses knew the road that they would take to the place where they intended to sacrifice. Thus when Pharaoh heard that the Israelites started to go by way of the wilderness, and when they had traveled some distance backtracked to go in another way, Pharaoh surmised that everything that Moses had told him was said in guile, that he did not intend to sacrifice but to flee. For one who flees becomes confused on the way and does not know which road to take.

OVER AGAINST IT. The word nikhcho (over against it) is vocalized with a chirik . It is similar to the word niflo (was fallen) in after that he was fallen (II Sam. 1:10). There are many other such instances.
AND PHARAOH WILL SAY OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. This is similar to say of me (Gen. 20:13).

ENTANGLED. Nevukhim (entangled) is vocalized with a shuruk in place of a cholam . It is similar to the word ta’avuri (pass) in neither pass from hence (Ruth 2:8), for nevukhim is a nifal as the word nekhonim (ready) (Ex. 19:11) is. Now navokhu (perplexed) (Joel 1:18) and also navokhah (perplexed) in but the city of Shushan was perplexed (Est. 3:15) are like nakhonah (established) in And the kingdom was established (I Kings 2:46). Its meaning is, they are like a person who cannot find anyone to advise him and does not know what to do. The nun in nivkhe (depths of) in the depths of the sea (Job 38:16) is a root letter. The meaning of nivkhe yam (the springs of the sea) is the depths of the sea. Nivkhe has no place here.
THE WILDERNESS HATH SHUT THEM IN. The ways of the wilderness are closed to them, and like fugitives they do not know where to go.
AND I WILL HARDEN PHARAOH’S HEART. As if he forgot the plagues with which the Egyptians were smitten because of Israel.
AND I WILL GET ME HONOR UPON PHARAOH. My glory shall be manifest in the world when I drown Pharaoh and his army.
AND THE EGYPTIANS SHALL KNOW. The remnants and those who drowned prior to their death shall know that I am the Lord .
AND THEY DID SO. Scripture’s short way of saying that they turned backwards.
AND IT WAS TOLD THE KING OF EGYPT. That they are not going for any purpose but to flee.
AND HE MADE READY HIS CHARIOT. By command. It is like So Solomon built the house (I Kings 14:4).
AND HE TOOK SIX HUNDRED CHOSEN CHARIOTS. The chosen chariots of all the chariots that he had.

AND CAPTAINS. Note that the king is like the number one. Therefore the one who is next to him in rank is called the mishneh (the second), which is derived from the same root as shenayim (two). The third in rank is called the shelishi .
WITH A HIGH HAND. They had all the weapons of war and so did not go out like fugitives.

AND THE EGYPTIANS PURSUED AFTER THEM. This is in keeping with linguistical style. It is similar to and the people saw , and they trembled and stood far off (Ex. 20:15), the meaning of which is, when they saw this, they trembled and stood far off. The meaning of and the Egyptians pursued after them thus is: when the Egyptians pursued them, they overtook them as they were encamping by the sea.
[ALL THE HORSES.] Scripture notes this to inform us that they did not come upon them scattered.
AND HIS HORSEMEN. Parashav means his horsemen.
AND HIS ARMY. Chelo (his army) means his foot soldiers.
AND WHEN PHARAOH DREW NEAR. When Pharaoh caused his camp to draw near. The verb hikriv (drew near) is always transitive in Scripture.

AND THEY SAID. We find that the holy tongue employs two words with one meaning back to back when one would suffice. Now the phrase ha-mibbeli en kevarim (because there were no graves) is similar to ha-rak akh be-mosheh (only with Moses?) (Num. 12:2).
TO BRING US FORTH. Le-hotzi’anu (to bring us forth) is vocalized with a long kamatz in place of a tzere . It is similar to ro’ani (seeth me) in Thou hast said : None seeth me (Is. 47:10).

IS THIS NOT THE WORD. This is not stated. However, we know that this was the case, for how could they say to his face something that was not true? This remark was included in but they hearkened not unto Moses (Ex. 6:9).

STAND STILL, AND SEE THE SALVATION OF THE LORD. For you will not wage war but you shall see the salvation which the Lord will work for you this day. One may ask: How is it that a large camp comprising six hundred thousand armed men were afraid of those who pursued them? Why did they not stand and fight for their own and their children’s lives? The answer is: The Egyptians were masters over Israel. The generation that left Egypt were trained from their youth to bear the yoke of the Egyptians. They were of humble spirit. How then could they now wage war against their masters? The Israelites were lazy and not learned in war. Can you not see that were it not for the prayers of Moses, the Amalekites, who came with a small number of men, would have defeated Israel. God alone, Who doeth great things (Job 5:9); And by Him actions are weighed (I Sam. 2:3), so arranged events that all Israelite males who left Egypt died out, for they had no spirit to fight the Canaanites; and a new generation with a noble spirit, who had never tasted exile, arose after the generation of the wilderness. I have noted the aforementioned in the account of Moses recorded in the Torah portion Ve-Eleh Shemot .

THE LORD WILL FIGHT FOR YOU. Lakhem means for you. Similarly, whenever the word war ( milchamah ) is followed by a lamed it indicates aid. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen therefore explains li (me) in For there are many that fight (lochamim) me (li) on high (Ps. 56:3) to mean for me. The meaning of on high is, a war on high, as is the case with all that sit.
AND YE SHALL HOLD YOUR PEACE. In contrast to and the children of Israel cried out (v. 10).

WHEREFORE CRIEST THOU UNTO ME. Some say that Moses was crying out unto the Lord. However, this is incorrect, for God had already told Moses, and I will get Me honor upon Pharaoh (v. 4). On the contrary, this was told to Moses who stood in Israel’s stead because the children of Israel cried out to the Lord.
THAT THEY GO FORWARD. Little by little until they reach the edge of the sea.

AND LIFT THOU UP. God told Moses to lift up his rod and divide the sea before the children of Israel went forward. The Lord did not tell Moses to strike the sea. He told him to stretch out his hand toward the sea in the manner of And Moses stretched forth his rod toward heaven (Ex. 9:23). We know that the rod did not divide the sea but that from the moment that Moses stretched his hand toward the sea God caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind and the waters then split. For it is so written.

AND I. We know that the Red Sea is not situated between Egypt and the Land of Israel. There was no reason for them to enter the sea. However, God commanded them to do so, so that the Egyptians would enter behind them and drown. The children of Israel, as I will explain, entered the sea from the wilderness of Etham and exited the sea to the wilderness of Etham.
AND THE EGYPTIANS SHALL KNOW. Those that remained.
WHEN I HAVE GOTTEN ME HONOR UPON PHARAOH. Who will drown along with his chariots and horsemen.

AND THE ANGEL OF GOD. This took place before speak unto the children of Israel, that they should go forward (v. 15). It’s meaning thus is, and the angel of God had already removed. I have already showed you many such instances. Now because these three verses are connected to each other and each one has seventy-two letters we find in them, as stated in the books, the sign of the secret of God’s explicit name. However, in my opinion it is so written because, as I will explain in the Torah portion Ki Tissa , the numerical value of God’s glorious name comes to seventy-two. The Book of Raziel states that one who wants to query the heavenly powers in a dream should read the verse, Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year , etc. (Ezek. 1:1), for it contains seventy-two letters.

THE ANGEL OF GOD. The reference is to the great prince who goes in the cloud, concerning whom it is written, And the Lord went before them by day (Ex. 13:21). When this angel, who went before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them, the pillar of cloud moved with him. Let the one who identifies the angel of God with the cloud show us where we find the pillar of cloud called the angel of God. Furthermore, if the angel and the pillar are one and the same, why is and the pillar of cloud removed from before them repeated? If he should answer that Scripture repeats the same idea in different words, then we respond that it is not the manner of Scripture to repeat itself except in prophecy or reproof. Moreover, it is unfit to repeat oneself when reporting how something happened.
AND IT CAME. And the angel came.
AND THERE WAS THE CLOUD AND THE DARKNESS HERE. Between the camps.

AND IT LIT UP THE NIGHT. As was the manner on all the nights, so that Israel could cross the sea. They crossed it at night. Rabbi Merinus says that the meaning of va-ya’er (he lit up) is, he darkened. And the night shall be light about me (Ps. 139: 11) is similar. Furthermore, we find, On the light of the fourteenth day in rabbinic literature. However, the one who interprets thus turns darkness into light and light into darkness, for it is impossible in any language for a word to mean both a thing and its opposite unless it is euphemistically used, as in Naboth did bless God and the king (I Kings 21:13). The word light in shall be light about me refers to the light itself, as I have explained. Similarly, the sages said that On the light of the fourteenth is a refined language, which is similar to a euphemism. Furthermore, what reason was there for Scripture to say, and he darkened the night ? It is dark every night. The only meaning of va-ya’er et ha-laylah is that he lit up the night as he did from the day that Israel went out of Egypt, for the pillar of fire was seen every night. Now if Israel had no light how did they cross the sea? For behold, by the time Pharaoh came into the sea and the Lord looked forth upon him in the morning watch, most of the Israelites had already crossed.
AND MOSES STRETCHED OUT HIS HAND…ALL THE NIGHT. Even while Israel was crossing, the wind did not cease.

AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL WENT INTO THE MIDST OF THE SEA. Do not think that because Scripture reads, in the midst of the sea that the Israelites reached the middle of the Red Sea. On the contrary, even if they entered the sea for even half of a Persian mile one may say that they came in the midst of the sea. It is like And the mixed multitude that was in the midst of them (Num. 11:4), for the mixed multitude was not in the middle of the camp. The meaning of the midst of the sea is, the place where there was water at the beginning of the night.

AND THE WATERS WERE A WALL UNTO THEM. The waters froze. It is also written, The floods stood upright as a heap (Ex. 15:8). After most of Israel crossed, the waters which formed a wall for them melted. This is the meaning of that the waters may come back upon the Egyptians (v. 26). These waters separated between the Egyptians and the dry land. It therefore states, and the Egyptians fled against it (v. 27), as the Egyptians thought that they would go out onto dry land. But the walls of water melted and separated them and dry land. There is no doubt that those who pursued Israel saw the light by which Israel crossed.
AND IT CAME TO PASS IN THE MORNING WATCH. The alef of ashmoret (watch) is a superfluous letter.

THAT THE LORD LOOKED FORTH. The reference is to the angel of the Lord mentioned earlier. The same is the case with Gideon, where the messenger is called by the name of the sender. Since the sender commands his agent to commit an act, it is as if the sender himself had executed it.
THROUGH THE PILLAR OF FIRE AND OF CLOUD. Between these two pillars.

AND DISCOMFITED. Possibly because of this the poet says, The voice of Thy thunder was in the whirlwind (Ps. 77:19). Similarly And He shot forth lightnings, and discomfited them (Ps. 18:15). Elsewhere it is written, And He sent…Lightning, and discomfited them (II Sam. 22:15).
AND HE TOOK OFF. Va-yasar (and He took off) is a hifil . It should have been vocalized va-yaser with a segol beneath the samekh . I have already noted its grammatical explanation.

[AND HE TOOK OFF THEIR CHARIOT WHEELS.] Some say its meaning is that they untied the knot of the wheel from the horses so that, being lighter, they could flee more easily. However, the above-mentioned divine discomfit fell upon them and their horses, and they could only drive them with great difficulty. Others say that va-yasar comes from the root of sorer (rebellious) (Deut. 21:18). He who went before them wanted to turn the chariot around.

FOR THE LORD FIGHTETH FOR THEM AGAINST THE EGYPTIANS. Lahem means for them. It now becomes clear that God’s word, and the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord (v. 4), which He spoke earlier meant: and the Egyptians shall know before their deaths.
THAT THE WATERS MAY COME BACK. The waters which served as walls for them should return to their previous state.
WHEN THE MORNING APPEARED. Lifnot boker (when the morning appeared) means toward morning.
TO ITS STRENGTH. Le-etano means to its strength. It is a noun, like etan in mighty rivers (Ps. 74:15).

FLED AGAINST IT. I have already explained that the Egyptians in fleeing thought that they were returning to dry land when in actuality they were going toward the sea. May the bones of Chivi the dog be crushed. Chivi said that Moses knew the time of low tide, when the level of the sea goes down, and the time of high tide, when the sea comes in and its level rises, and so brought his people across the sea when the tide was normally low. However, Pharaoh did not know the manner of the sea and therefore drowned. This interpretation is sheer madness, as the sea is not normally dry in any place when its level goes down. However, all was dry. Neither do walls of water remain on the right or the left. Furthermore, the end of low tide and the beginning of high tide do not become clear until some hours have passed. Moreover, the Israelites had not yet finished crossing before Pharaoh and his army drowned.

AND THE LORD OVERTHREW. Va-yena’er (overthrew) is a pi’el. Na’arti (I shook) in Also I shook out my lap (Neh. 5:13) is similar to it. Va-yena’er is to be understood in the manner of hath He thrown into the sea (Ex. 15: 1).
AND THE WATERS RETURNED. The waters that were walls returned.

SO MUCH AS ONE OF THEM. Even one of them did not escape. Similarly ad echad in and, behold, there was not so much as one (ad echad) of the cattle of the Israelites dead (Ex. 9:7). Indeed, the poet says, There was not one of them (echad me-hem) left (Ps. 106: 11).

BUT THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. The reason this is noted a second time is that there remained some Israelites who were still crossing the sea while Pharaoh was drowning. This was a miracle within a miracle, for in the place where the Israelites were crossing the sea there was a strong east wind drying and where Pharaoh and his host were, God brought another wind to melt the waters that were frozen and formed walls. There were thus two winds in two places in the sea close to one another. True proof that this interpretation is correct is offered by the statement in the Song of Moses, And with the blast of Thy nostrils the waters were piled up (Ex. 15:8), which speaks of the wind that blew for Israel; and the statement, Thou didst blow with Thy wind, the sea covered them (Ex. 15:10), which speaks of the wind that caused the Egyptians to drown. It is because of this that the end of the song reads, and the Lord brought back the waters of the sea upon them; but the children of Israel walked on dry land in the midst of the sea (Ex. 15:19). Do not ask, how could all of Israel cross in one night? Did not the six hundred thousand men on foot make up only a quarter of the camp? Perhaps they passed over some other way. Or perhaps the sea split into twelve parts, as the sages of blessed memory say. Now the Israelites did not cross the width of the sea. On the contrary, they moved along its length and came out in the wilderness of Shur from wherein, as I will explain, they entered the sea.

THUS THE LORD SAVED. Now the Israelites were saved from the hand of the Egyptians. Until now the fear of Pharaoh was upon them. Scripture tells us that the Egyptians drowned in the sea. The sea did not cast their bodies out upon the dry land, for it is clearly written, The earth swallowed them (Ex. 15:12). The meaning of and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea-shore therefore is: when the Egyptians drowned, the Israelites, who were on the shore, saw their dead bodies.
FEARED. When Israel saw this great blow they feared God, as in And David was afraid of the Lord that day when Uzzah who put forth his hand to the ark of God died (II Sam. 6:9).
AND THEY BELIEVED IN THE LORD. They believed that the Lord is truth and that Moses is His servant and will do only that which the Lord commands him to do.

THEN SANG MOSES. It is Hebrew style to employ an imperfect preceded by the word az (then) in place of a perfect. Compare, Az yivneh shelomoh (then did Solomon build) (I Kings 11:7); az yedabber yehoshu’a (then spoke Joshua) (Josh. 10:12); az yavdil mosheh (then Moses separated) (Deut. 4:41). The same is true in Arabic. Moses composed the song by himself. He then taught it to all of Israel, each one of whom then sang and said, I will sing unto the Lord . And Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people (Deut. 27:1) is similar. The commandment was first spoken only by Moses. The elders of Israel then repeated it to everyone.
AND SPOKE, SAYING. Each one of the Israelites was to say the following, or the following was to be said in every generation.

FOR HE IS HIGHLY EXALTED. He demonstrated His exaltation by casting both the mighty rider and his exalted and powerful steed into the sea as one casts an arrow. The meaning of ramah (thrown) in ramah va-yam (hath He thrown into the sea) is similar to the word rome (throws) in armed with that which a bow throws (Ps. 78:9).

THE LORD IS MY STRENGTH AND SONG. Rabbi Solomon of blessed memory says that there is a difference between ozzi (my strength), which is vocalized with a furtive kamatz , and uzzi , which is vocalized with a kubbutz . He therefore says that the yod in ozzi (my strength) in the Lord is my strength and song is superfluous. However, Rabbi Solomon does not offer another such instance. Rabbi Solomon goes on to say that ve-zimrat (and song) is in the construct with Yah (the Lord). He interprets our verse as if it read: The strength and vengeance of the Lord became my salvation. Rabbi Solomon thought that our verse is similar to va-yehi ba-yom ha-shelishi va-yissa avraham et enav (on the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes) (Gen. 22:4). However, one who knows Arabic knows the difference between the two verses. It is neither correct Hebrew nor Arabic form to say ozzi ve-zimrat Yah va-yehi li li-shu’ah . There is no difference between ozzi vocalized with a furtive kamatz and the same word vocalized with a kubbutz . For while Scripture reads, chukki (mine allotted) in Feed me with mine allotted bread (Prov. 30:8) it elsewhere reads, chokkha ve-chok ba-nekha (thy due, and thy son’s due) (Lev. 10:13). Now we find the word ve-ozzekha (in Thy strength) (v. 13) vocalized with a furtive kamatz, later on in this song and similarly in O Lord, in Thy strength (be-ozzekha) the king re-joiceth (Ps. 21:2). The yod of ozzi is thus a first person suffix. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen says that the meaning of ve-zimrat Yah is, the Lord is my song, for the resh of ve-zimrat (and song) is vocalized with a kamatz . Similarly, the meaning of shenat in I will not give sleep (shenat) to mine eyes (Ps. 132:4) is, my sleep, as shenat is vocalized with a kamatz . Likewise, the meaning of nachalat, which is vocalized with a kamatz in Yea, I have a goodly heritage (nachalat) (Ps. 16:6) is my heritage. Similarly, the meaning of menat, which is vocalized with a kamatz in, O Lord, the portion (menat) of mine inheritance and of my cup (Ps. 16:5), is my portion. However, what will Rabbi Moses do with the word menat (portion) in the king’s portion (II Chron. 31:3) in which menat is vocalized with a kamatz and is in the construct. It is the same case with the word yam (sea) in the salt sea (Num. 34:3) and in the sea (yam) of Chinnereth (Num. 34:11). Should one respond that the latter are irregular, we would tell him to place ozzi ve-zimrat Yah among them. I believe that the word ozzi (my strength) is, as is the style of the Hebrew language, to be read as if written twice. Our clause is to be read as if written, ozzi, ve-zimrat ozzi Yah (The Lord is my strength and the song of my strength). The reason behind this verse is that Moses earlier mentioned, The horse and his rider hath He thrown into the sea (v. 4). Moses now states that this was not through his own majesty and strength. On the contrary, he confesses, my strength and the glory of my strength is Yah alone who is the Lord. Yah is, as I have explained, one of the three proper names of God. All three come from one root. Since the word eheyeh is frequently employed in speech it was necessary to substitute a vav for a yod in God’s glorious name. The word Yah is likewise known. Its yod was vocalized with a pattach because of the guttural and the silent yod was dropped because it has another secret numerical meaning. We find Yah combined with God’s glorious name in ki ozzi ve-zimrat Yah YHVH (for God the Lord is my strength and song) (Is. 12:2). I have already explained that the name YHVH is at times a proper name and at times an adjective.
THIS IS MY GOD. My power.
AND I WILL GLORIFY HIM. I will place Him in a building.

[THIS.] The word zeh (this) is to be read as if written twice. The last clause of our verse is to be read as if written: And this is my father’s God, the reference being to the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
AND I WILL EXALT HIM. For I will recount His might.
THE LORD IS A MAN OF WAR. The Lord supports those who love Him and cleave unto Him and He is a man of war to their enemies.

[MAN.] The word ish (man) means a being. Scripture thus states in reference to the stars, ish lo nedar (not one faileth) (Is. 40:26); and in reference to the living creatures, ish el ever panav yelekhu (they went every one straight forward) (Ezek. 1:9); and in reference to the angels, ve-ha-ish gavriel (the man Gabriel) (Dan. 9:21). The meaning of ish milchamah (a man of war) thus is, a being who wages war. It is similar to the term ish emunim (a faithful man) (Prov. 20:6), the meaning of which is, a being imbued with faith.

THE LORD IS HIS NAME. His name will now be known. Compare, That calleth for the waters of the sea, And poureth them out upon the face of the earth; The Lord is His name (Amos 5:8). He alone can do such a thing.
PHARAOH’S CHARIOTS. God, as it were, cast Pharaoh’s heavy chariots and their hosts as if they were a light arrow.
[AND HIS CHOSEN CAPTAINS.] Moses made mention of his chosen captains “who were over all them” because he had previously spoken of Pharaoh’s hosts.

[THE RED SEA.] Yefet says that suf in yam suf (the Red Sea) has the same meaning as the word suf (flags) in The reeds and flags shall wither (Is. 19:6) and the word suf in and laid it in the flags (Ex. 2:3). For reeds and rushes grow around the yam suf , and not around other seas. However, Rabbi Joshua says that suf is the name of a city. It is like yam kinneret (the sea of Chinnereth) (Josh. 13:27).
THE DEEPS. The deeps of the earth. Compare, The earth swallowed them (v. 11).
[COVER THEM.] A shuruk has been substituted for a cholam in yekhasyumu (cover them). Compare, ta’avuri (pass) in neither pass from hence (Ruth 2:8).
THE DEPTHS. Metzolot (the depths) means the deep waters. Similarly va-tashlikheni metuzlah, (for thou did cast me into the deep waters) (Jonah 2:4).
GLORIOUS. The yod of nedari (glorious) is superfluous. It is like the yod of akhzari (cruel).

[THY RIGHT HAND.] The repetition of the phrase Thy right hand, O Lord indicates the same as the repetition of For, lo, Thine enemies, O Lord (Ps. 92:10) and The floods have lifted up (Ps. 93:3). It indicates time and time again. Its meaning is: your right hand dashes the enemy in pieces times without number.
[GLORIOUS IN POWER.] Glorious in power refers to God. However, there are those who say that it refers to the Lord’s right hand.

AND IN THE GREATNESS OF THY EXCELLENCE. Which is superior to all who exalt themselves. You are able to shatter (overthrow) those that rise up against You. You need no iron weapons to shatter them. All You have to do is send forth Your wrath and it consumeth them as stubble, for God’s wrath is as hot as fire.
AND WITH THE BLAST OF THY NOSTRILS. You rebuke the waters and they congeal. Compare, By the breath of God they perish (Job 4:9).
THE WATERS WERE PILED UP. The word ne’ermu (were piled up) is similar to the word aremat (a heap of) in a heap of wheat (Cant. 7:3).
THE FLOODS STOOD UPRIGHT AS A HEAP. The waters, whose nature is to flow and descend, turned into a heap ( ned ), as in And rose up in one heap (ned) (Josh. 4:16). The meaning of ned (heap) is a wall.
THE DEEPS WERE CONGEALED. Kafe’u means were congealed. Compare, ve-kippa’on (frost) (Zech. 14:6).
IN THE HEART OF THE SEA. The heart lies in the middle of the body from the point of view of the body’s width.
THE ENEMY SAID. The reference is to Pharaoh.

[SHALL BE SATISFIED UPON THEM.] The word timla’emo (shall be satisfied upon them) is difficult. Rabbi Merinus explains that timla’emo nafshi (my lust shall be satisfied upon them) means: my person shall be full of them; i.e., I will take all of their wealth. The term timla’emo is to be understood like the term yetza’uni (gone forth of me) in My children are gone forth of me (Jer. 10:20). Its meaning is connected to I will divide the spoil . Others say that timla’emo is used in the same sense as the word me’lo’o (presume) in that durst presume in his heart (Esth. 7:5).
[MY HAND SHALL DESTROY THEM.] After doing the latter I shall destroy them.
MY HAND SHALL DESTROY THEM. Torishemo means shall destroy them. Similarly the word torishu (you will destroy) in But if you will not destroy (Num. 34:55).

THOU DIDST BLOW WITH THY WIND. Nashafta (Thou didst blow) comes from the same root as neshef (night). The meaning of nashafta ve-ruchakha (Thou didst blow with Thy wind) is: You brought a wind at night that drowned them.
THEY SANK. Tzalelu (they sank) comes from the same root as metzolot (depths). Compare, My lips quivered (tzalelu) at the voice (Hab. 3:16).
IN THE MIGHTY WATERS. This is connected to they sank. Our verse is to be read as if written: they sank as lead in the mighty waters.

AS LEAD. Oferet (lead) comes from the same root as afar (dust). If one puts any of the six kinds of metal in the ground each will lose one of its familiar elements in a given number of years. However, lead will always maintain itself.

WHO IS LIKE UNTO THEE, O LORD, AMONG THE MIGHTY. Elim (the mighty) refers to the holy angels in the celestial heights. The sons of the mighty (bene elim) refers to the stars. I will explain this further in the Torah portion Ki Tissa.
GLORIOUS IN HOLINESS. The reference is to the Throne of Glory.

[FEARFUL IN PRAISES, DOING WONDERS.] For all who want to acclaim God are afraid to praise His name because who can recite all of His praises. However, they are obligated to praise Him because He alone does wonders.

THOU STRETCHEDST OUT THY RIGHT HAND. Your wonders were manifest when You stretched forth Your hand from the highest realm of the celestial heights where Your name is exalted, and the ground which is beneath all earthly creatures swallowed up the enemy of Israel. Your right hand, which is above the heaven of heavens, reached, as it were, in a moment to the bottom of the sea.
[THY RIGHT HAND.] Its meaning is, Thy strength.
THOU IN THY LOVE HAST LED. Moses used the perfect nachita (led) in place of the imperfect, as is the style in prophecy.
[IN THY LOVE.] The reference is to the pillars of cloud and fire, for God led them. On the other hand, it might allude to the fact that God led them up till now.
THOU HAST LED. Nehalta (thou hast led) is similar to etnahalah (I will journey) in I will lead on gently (Gen. 33:14).
IN THY STRENGTH. Not by their strength.
TO THY HOLY HABITATION. The reference is to Mount Sinai where God’s Glory dwelt. It is similarly written, and brought you unto Myself (Ex. 19:4).
THE PEOPLES HAVE HEARD. The reference is to the peoples round about them and also to the peoples whom they would pass by.
PANGS HAVE TAKEN HOLD ON THE INHABITANTS OF PHILISTIA. The inhabitants of the land of Philistia. The word inhabitants indicates this.
THE MIGHTY MEN. Ele (mighty men) spelled with a yod means sheep, for the sheep have leaders.

[THEN WERE THE CHIEFS OF EDOM AFFRIGHTED…THE MIGHTY MEN OF MOAB, TREMBLING TAKETH HOLD UPON THEM.] The Philistines, the Edomites, and the Moabites did not wage war with the Israelites in the wilderness.

ALL THE INHABITANTS OF CANAAN ARE MELTED AWAY. Because of the reports which they received, as in And as soon as we heard it, our hearts did melt (Josh. 2:11). The inhabitants of Canaan is also to be interpreted as the inhabitants of the land of Canaan.

TERROR AND DREAD FALLETH UPON THEM. This refers to Edom and Moab even though Canaan is mentioned above. He spoke unto them in a pillar of cloud (Ps. 99:79) is, as I have explained, similar. Likewise, and shed the blood of war in peace (I Kings 2:5) only refers to Abner. So too, and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his maid-servants; and they bore children refers to Abimelech’s wife and handmaids. All of this because Scripture reads, Till thy people pass over, O Lord . For Israel passed them before they came to the land of Canaan. Moses repeated Till Thy people pass because they circled Mount Seir for many days.
[THOU HAST GOTTEN.] Its meaning is: they were slaves in Egypt and Thou hast gotten them to be Your servants.

THOU BRINGEST THEM IN, AND PLANTEST THEM IN THE MOUNTAIN OF THINE INHERITANCE. A prayer that Israel remain long in the land and not be exiled from it. Our verse is like in the mountain of the height of Israel will I plant it (Ezek. 17:23).
IN THE MOUNTAIN. The goodly hill country and Lebanon (Deut. 3:25) is similar. Or it alludes to Mount Moriah. It is therefore followed by The place, O Lord, which Thou hast made for Thee to dwell in.

[WHICH THOU HAST MADE.] Its meaning is: which Thou hast prepared as a place for a sanctuary for Thyself. The place mentioned lies opposite the glorious celestial place, for the places on earth vary in accordance with the star that is over them. Those who are versed in the science that deals with the constellations will understand this.

[THE SANCTUARY.] The word mikkedash (sanctuary) has the same meaning as mikdash (sanctuary). The word mittoharo (his brightness) in Thou hast made his brightness to cease (Ps. 89:45) is similar, as the dagesh in the tet is superfluous, like the dagesh in the kof of mikkedash . The dalet does not receive a dagesh because the kof is vocalized with a mobile sheva . With the exception of the form shetayim we do not find it to be the way of Scripture to place a dagesh in a word which follows a mobile sheva. I have already noted its grammatical uniqueness.
WHICH THY HANDS HAVE ESTABLISHED. Its meaning is similar to thou hast made, for Scripture repeats itself.
THE LORD SHALL REIGN. God’s Kingship will be seen when the Holy Temple which will be dedicated to His name shall be built.

[FOR EVER AND EVER.] Le-olam va-ed (for ever and ever) is an abridgment. The full form is le-olam ve-ad olam (for ever and until ever). Do not be amazed that the word ed is not in the construct, for we find, shokhen ad ve-kadosh shemo (That inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy) (Is. 57:15). It is the custom of Hebrew to vocalize a vav with a pattach when the syllable which follows it is accented. Compare, va-ez (or goat) in of ox, or sheep, or goat (Lev. 7:23). It is for this reason that va-ed is vocalized with a pattach . Now Scripture reads, va-okhal mi-kol (I have eaten of all) (Gen. 27:33). However, at the end of a verse it reads, ha-nachash hishi’ani va-okhel (the serpent beguiled me, and I did eat) (Gen. 3:13). Hence the statement, le-olam va-ed .
FOR THE HORSES OF PHARAOH. This verse is, in my opinion, part of the song. Its purpose is to recall the wonder within the wonder, which I have noted.

[UPON THEM.] Upon them refers to the horses of Pharaoh…his chariots and his horsemen. It also includes Pharaoh. For Scripture clearly states, The enemy (Pharaoh) said (v. 9) and then goes on to say, The earth swallowed them (v. 12). Furthermore, it is explicitly written, But (God) overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red Sea (Ps. 136:15).

AND MOSES LED. I believe that the pillar of cloud, and likewise the pillar of fire, that went before the people when they left Egypt was to ensure that Israel was able to go by day and by night (Ex. 13:21). After Pharaoh and his hosts drowned, Israel was no longer frightened and did not travel at night. Indeed, we do not find it recorded in the Torah portion Be-Halotekha that Israel journeyed at night. Behold, Moses now led the people according to God’s command. There are only six journeys from the Red Sea until Mount Sinai lasting less than forty days. The air is then good. It is neither humid nor cold. He who does not have a tent can live outdoors without harm. When Israel came to the wilderness of Sinai they all erected booths, as they camped there for about year. Moses informed them that they would tarry there until they constructed the Tabernacle. It was for this reason that, as I will explain, Israel brought out acacia wood from Egypt. The festival of booths was established in commemoration of the booths that Israel made there, for Scripture states, that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt (Lev. 23:43). How can one maintain that Israel dwelt in clouds? For the booths do not resemble clouds. I will yet explain why the festival of Sukkot is observed in the seventh month. When the Tabernacle was erected God descended upon it in a pillar of cloud, as it is clearly written, and there was fire therein by night (Ex. 40:38). When the cloud journeyed the children of Israel went onward (Ex. 40:36). It is because of this that Scripture reads, and thou goest before them, in a pillar of cloud by day (Num. 14:14). There were thus two interchanging pillars over the Tabernacle. If the statement to the effect that there were seven interchanging pillars over the Tabernacle is based on tradition, then we will rely on tradition and set aside our own opinions.

INTO THE WILDERNESS OF SHUR. This is the very wilderness of Etham. Perhaps there were two cities in the wilderness that were so called. Or the wilderness had two names. And they went three days in the wilderness, the reference being to the wilderness of Shur, is proof of this. Therefore to indicate this the bet of ba-midbar (in the wilderness), which precedes and found no water, was vocalized for emphasis with a pattach .

AND WHEN THEY CAME TO MARAH. It is elsewhere written, And they journeyed from the Red Sea (Num. 33:11). The latter is similar to And Moses led Israel onward from the Red Sea , ( and they went out into the wilderness of Shur and came to Marah ) (v. 22). We similarly find, and they went three days’ journey in the wilderness of Etham, and pitched in Marah (Num. 33:8).
THEREFORE THE NAME OF IT WAS CALLED MARAH. Someone called it Marah. Who was born unto Levi in Egypt (Num. 26:29) is similar.

AND THE PEOPLE MURMURED. Va-yillonu (murmured) is a nifal. It is similar to ve-yikkonu (shall be established) in And thy thoughts shall be established (Prov. 16:3), which comes from the same root as nakhonu (prepared) (Prov. 19:29). It comes from a double root or from a root in which the middle letter is missing. If it came from a root which begins with a nun it would have followed the paradigm of va-yiggashu (came near) (Gen. 45:4).

AND HE CRIED UNTO THE LORD; AND THE LORD SHOWED HIM A TREE. We do not know what type of tree this was. What happened can only be described as a miracle. If the waters were stationary then we would say that they were medicinally sweetened. What the sages said is correct.
THERE HE MADE FOR THEM. God for Israel.
A STATUTE AND AN ORDINANCE. To discipline them and to instruct them.

[AND THERE HE PROVED THEM.] This is to be understood in the manner of for the Lord your God putteth you to proof, to know whether ye do love the Lord your God with all you heart and with all your soul (Deut. 13:4). Scripture similarly states, And He afflicted thee, and suffered thee to hunger (Deut. 8:3); and that He might prove thee, to do thee good at thy latter end (Deut. 8:16), that is, to do good to those who did not murmur against Moses.

AND HE SAID: IF THOU WILT DILIGENTLY HEARKEN. I have already noted that when the word shema (hearken) is followed by a lamed or a bet it does not mean to hear the words being spoken but rather to understand the subject which is being verbalized. Shema in our verse thus means to understand what the Lord commands us to do.
AND WILT DO THAT WHICH IS RIGHT IN HIS EYES. This refers to the positive commandments.
AND WILT GIVE EAR TO HIS COMMANDMENTS. To understand what the negative commandments consist of.
AND KEEP ALL HIS STATUTES. Not to violate them. Compare, And ye shall not walk in the statutes of the nation (Lev. 20:23). It is God’s statute not to imitate the practices of the nations.

[NONE OF THE DISEASES.] Its meaning is, the diseases you should remember. For you saw with your own eyes the diseases, the strokes, and the plagues which I put upon the Egyptians because they rebelled against Me. Now if you will hearken to My statutes you will be saved from these plagues, for I will not do to you what I did to them. Additionally, you have no need of a physician for I am the Lord that healeth thee from all disease which I have decreed to be upon the earth. I will heal you as I healed the bitter waters which no physician has the ability to heal. Behold, what happened at Marah was the opposite of what occurred when the first plague struck, for the waters of the Nile were sweet but the Egyptians could not drink from them. However, here the bitter waters turned sweet. You should therefore love the Lord and keep yourself from rebelling against Him, for He will do good for you.

AND THEY CAME TO ELIM. Saadiah Gaon says there were seventy species of palm trees there. Others added, for each and every tribe. Others said, for each and every person. However, there is no need for these interpretations, for the springs of water, of which there were twelve, and the seventy palm trees did not come into being now because of Israel. Additionally, this was not the time for the ripening of palms. I believe that Israel tarried in Marah for only one day and that they stayed in Elim for about twenty days. Scripture therefore says, and they encamped there by the waters . The next verse therefore informs us that Israel journeyed from Elim on the fifteenth day of the second month. Now Israel camped in the following four places in fifteen days: the wilderness of Sinai, Dophkah, Alush, and Rephidim, for they came to the desert of Sinai at the beginning of the third month. Scripture mentions the palm trees to let us know that contrary to the waters of Marah the waters here were sweet, for palm trees cannot flourish in a land of bitter waters.

AND THEY TOOK THEIR JOURNEY. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says that the reason Scripture mentions the fifteenth day of the second month is to inform us that Israel left Egypt on the fifth day of the week. Now, the first day of Nisan fell on a Thursday and Iyyar on a Friday and on a Sabbath. Israel came to the wilderness of Sin on a Sabbath and complained upon camping. Moses then told them that they would eat meat at even and that manna would come down in the morning. Now it is logical to assume that the manna first came down on a Sunday because Scripture states, And it shall come to pass on the sixth day (v. 5), the reference being to the sixth day of the week and the sixth day from the day on which the manna began to descend. We will accept that which the Gaon says because of tradition, not because of his explanation, for who told the Gaon that the manna came down on the morning following the coming of the Israelites to the wilderness of Sin? The Israelites may have camped there for four or more days but the manna started to come down on Sunday. The latter is so because we start the count from the day that the manna began to fall, for all the nations rely on Israel with regard to this numeration. Observe, the Christians named the days of the week after the stars. However, they did not do the same with the Sabbath day. The first five days of the week in Arabic are numbered. The sixth day is called al juma because it is the most honored day of the week for the Arabs and they congregate on this day. The Arabs refer to the day of shabbat as sabbat because the shin and samekh interchange in their script. They learned this from the Israelites. Behold, the natives of India, who do not have the belief of six days of creation, begin the week on Wednesday because the sun is the star of that day and according to their beliefs it rules over them.

AND THE WHOLE CONGREGATION OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL MURMURED. The Israelites murmured only against Moses at the waters of Marah (Ex. 15:23) because it was he alone who led Israel onward. Only a part of Israel and not the whole nation complained. Scripture therefore reads, And the people murmured against Moses (Ex. 15:24). However, in the wilderness of Sin we find that Scripture states, And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron because both of them had brought them out of the land of Egypt. In Marah they complained because of the water. However, they now complained about a lack of bread and meat because they had already consumed most of their cattle, for thirty days had passed since they left Egypt. A congregation as large as Israel could only buy food at very great expense.
BEHOLD, I WILL CAUSE TO RAIN BREAD FROM HEAVEN. The bread will come down like rain from the sky.

[BREAD.] The word lechem (bread) means food. It is found used for bread itself and also for meat, as in lechem isheh (food of the offering made by fire) (Lev. 3:11). It is also used for fruit, as in Let us destroy the tree with the fruit thereof (be-lachmo) (Jer. 11:19).
[THAT I MAY PROVE THEM.] For they will daily need Me.
[TWICE.] The meaning of mishneh (twice) is two omers per person, for it is so written.

AND MOSES AND AARON SAID. Moses and Aaron said, then shall ye know that the Lord hath brought you out from the land of Egypt because the Israelites charged, for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness (v. 3). They answered, “Observe, we will perform two signs for you, one at the evening of this very day and one on the morning of the morrow so that you will know that the Lord hath brought you out from the land of Egypt .” Scripture should have read: at even and in the morning ye shall know because and in the morning is not connected to then ye shall see the glory of the Lord . For as Scripture goes on to say, Israel saw God’s glory on that very day.
AND IN THE MORNING. I have already explained this.
FOR THAT HE HATH HEARD YOUR MURMURINGS. This is connected to then ye shall see the glory of the Lord .
AND WHAT ARE WE. What can we do? We only did what we were commanded to do. The word ve-nachnu (and we) is missing an alef .
AND MOSES SAID. Moses now told them what the two signs would consist of.
COME NEAR BEFORE THE LORD. Turn to the wilderness.
AND IT CAME TO PASS. It became clear to them that when Aaron spoke to them, they came near before the Lord. The cloud came immediately and God’s glory was seen in it.
AND THE LORD SPOKE. The Israelites saw that Moses went to the glory of the Lord and spoke to God.

I HAVE HEARD. The word telunnot is irregular in that its nun has a dagesh . This prophecy is repeated. Scripture had already noted, the Lord shall give you in the evening flesh to eat, and in the morning bread to the full. It was only repeated so that Israel would see the glory of the Lord.

[AT DUSK.] The term ben ha-arbayim means, as I have already explained, at dusk. This verse proves my interpretation of and in the morning, then ye shall see the glory of God. (v. 7). For the verse states, At dusk ye shall eat flesh, and in the morning ye shall be filled with bread .
AND IT CAME TO PASS AT EVEN. At the end of that very day.
THAT THE QUAILS CAME UP. Possibly from the direction of the sea.

A LAYER OF DEW. Shikhvat (a layer) is similar to yashkiv (bring down) in Or who can bring down (yashkiv) the bottles of heaven (Job 38:37). It means a descent. Scripture elsewhere writes, u-veredet ha-tal (And when the dew descended) (Num. 11:9). May the name of Chivi rot for saying that the manna is to be identified with what is known in the Persian tongue as tarnagbin, in Arabic as man, and in the vernacular as manna. There are many questions raised against him. First of all, no manna falls today in the wilderness of Sinai, for we know the location of the mountain. Now I have seen that which resembles manna in the kingdom of Al tzakir, and it only comes down in Nisan and Iyyar and in no other months. Additionally, if you place it in the sun it does not melt. Furthermore, it does not rot in the evening. Moreover, it is not very hard and one does not have to grind it in a pestle if one wants to make cakes out of it. Furthermore, it melts when placed upon the tongue. In addition, it does not satisfy because it does not produce good blood. It is only used as a medical ingredient. Furthermore, a double portion of manna came down on Friday. Moreover, the manna did not come down on the Sabbath. Furthermore, the manna came down wherever Israel camped. In addition, the manna crossed over the Jordan with the Israelites and did not cease to descend, according to the plain meaning of Scripture, until half the month of Nisan, had passed.

AND WHEN THE LAYER OF DEW WAS GONE UP. The meaning of va-ta’al (was gone up) is ceased. It is similar to alah (went up) in Then defiledst thou it — my couch went up (alah) (Gen. 49:4). The meaning of the latter verse is: from the time that you defiled my couch it was removed from me and ceased to function. Ta’aleni (take me away) in O my God, take me not away in the midst of my days (Ps. 102:25) is similar. The dew came down first to clean the earth. When the dew was gone the manna descended. The latter is clearly written, viz., And when the dew fell upon the camp in the night, the manna fell upon it (Num. 11:9).

A FINE, SCALE-LIKE THING. Mechuspas (scale-like thing) means round shaped. It has no cognate. The one who says that mechuspas is similar to machsof (uncovering) (Gen. 30:37), which is spelled with a sin , is incorrect. For it is the manner of Hebrew to double the first and second root letters, as in the word yafyafita (thou art fairer) (Ps. 45:3), or to double the second and third stem letters, as in the word yerakrak (greenish) (Lev. 13:49), or to double only the third stem letter, as in sagrir (a very rainy day) (Prov. 27:15). However, we never find the second root letter doubled except for instances when the heh is silent, as in hagigi (my meditation) (Ps. 5:2) in which the gimel appears to be a third root letter after the heh is dropped. Hence it was doubled. However, we do not find the middle root letters to be doubled in words where all root letters are sounded.

AND WHEN THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL SAW IT. Rabbi Solomon says that the meaning of man hu (what is it) in Arabic is, what is it ? However, someone misinformed him, because the Arabic phrase for “what is it” is mah huwi, as the term man is used in Arabic exclusively in reference to people. The way to explain man is to note that it comes from the same root as minnah (appointed) in who hath appointed your food and your drink (Dan. 1:10).

[AND MOSES SAID UNTO THEM.] Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen says that we know that the Torah is not written in chronological order. Thus the meaning of And Moses said unto them is: and Moses had previously said unto them. There are many similar instances. Indeed, we find that Scripture states in this very portion, and it bred worms and rotted, the meaning of which is: and it bred worms and had previously rotted. Indeed, Scripture states, and it did not rot, neither was there any worm in it (v. 24). Scripture delayed reporting the words of Moses because it had to elaborate and go on to say, This is the thing which the Lord hath commanded, etc. (v. 16).
[GATHER YE OF IT EVERY MAN ACCORDING TO HIS EATING.] This was to be done by logical estimate. An omer for a head was for someone fully grown, for minors gather according to how much they consume.

AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL DID SO. According to the plain meaning of the text some gathered more and some less according to the number of people in their tents. However, our sages said that our verse speaks of a miracle.
AND WHEN THEY DID METE IT WITH AN OMER. Each one found that he had the amount that he had estimated.

AND MOSES SAID UNTO THEM: LET NO MAN LEAVE OF IT TILL THE MORNING. Its meaning is, do not leave some of the manna over to eat on the next morning. Rather, trust in the Lord that it will descend on the following day. There was no command to eat the entire omer. However, that which a person did not consume was to be thrown outside of his tent.

NOTWITHSTANDING THEY HEARKENED NOT UNTO MOSES. The word anashim (some of them) is connected to Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses . They were few in number. Rabbi Merinus says that va-yarum (and it bred worms) comes from the same root as rimmah (worms).
AND THEY GATHERED IT MORNING BY MORNING. The meaning of ve-cham ha-shemesh (and as the sun waxed hot) is: and when the day waxed hot. For the sun does not wax hot.
IT MELTED. Namas (melted) comes from a double root and is in the nifal.

AND IT CAME TO PASS. More than the usual amount of manna descended on this day, as Scripture goes on to note. Israel gathered twice as much food on this day because Moses had commanded them to do so. However, they did not know why. Also, Scripture states, they gathered, not they found. The rulers of the congregation came and told Moses that Israel did as he commanded them. They then asked Moses: What should be done with the extra portion? Why did he command them to gather twice as much food? How could they consume such a large amount of food?

AND HE SAID UNTO THEM. God has already told me that you are obligated to rest tomorrow and not do any work including the preparation of food, for tomorrow is a Sabbath day unto the Lord. This is God’s day because He rested from all His work on the seventh day. We find the same with regard to the Sabbatical year, viz., then shall the land keep a sabbath unto the Lord (Lev. 25:2).

[SABBATH.] The word shabbat is grammatically difficult. It does not belong in the paradigm of gannav (thief) because the tav of shabbat is a feminine suffix, as is proven by the phrase shabbat hi la-Adonai (it is a sabbath unto the Lord) (Lev. 23:3). The word shabbat is a noun meaning cessation. The following is its grammatical explanation. The word should have been spelled and vocalized shabbetet according to the paradigm of dalleket (inflammation) (Deut. 28:22). When one of the tavs was dropped the bet was vocalized with a kamatz to indicate that the word is feminine. It is the same, as I will explain, with the word achat (one).
[BAKE.] The word efu (bake) is irregular. It should have followed the paradigm of asu (do). Behold, Moses told the rulers of the congregation what they should do.

BAKE THAT WHICH YE WILL BAKE. Bake as you normally do so that you will have what to eat on this day. And see the that which ye will seethe has a similar meaning. Behold, prepare and cook all this according to your heart’s desire from one omer and eat as much as you need.

AND ALL THAT REMAINETH. Lay it up till the morning and I will tell you what to do. Now Moses did not inform them that no manna would descend on the Sabbath day. It was only in the morning that he revealed this secret to them

AND MOSES SAID. Many lacking in faith erred because of this verse and said that a person is obligated to keep the Sabbath day plus the night which follows it, because Moses said, for to-day and not the night before is a sabbath unto the Lord. Additionally, Moses said, Tomorrow is a solemn rest (v. 23). They interpreted, in accordance with their view, And there was evening and there was morning one day (Gen. 1:5) to mean that the first day was not finished until the morning of the second day. However, they spoke incorrectly. As I have already made mention to you, Moses spoke to Israel only in accordance with their practice. Now the manner of the land of the uncircumcised with regard to their food, their dress, their buildings, and affairs is not the same as that of the Land of Israel. It is the practice in the Land of Israel that no one bakes, cooks, or does any other work, both in summer or winter, at any time but during the day. Hence Moses said, Tomorrow is a solemn rest . Now pay close attention to understand the stupidity of those who explain and there was evening and there was morning in the manner which I noted above. For Scripture says, And God called the light day (Gen. 1:8), the reference being from the time that the sun rises until the time that it sets; and to the darkness He called night, the reference being from the time that the sun sets until the time that it rises. The night is thus the opposite of day, as the darkness is the opposite of the light. This being the case, how can Scripture refer to the evening, which commences at the time that the sun sets and lasts until the morning, as “day” when it is then night? Behold, concerning such people Scripture states, They change the night into day (Job 17:12). Now note that the word day is used in Hebrew in two ways. I have already mentioned one of them, viz., as long as the light of the sun is over any place on the earth. Therefore Scripture states, three days, night and day (Esth. 4:16) and, and night and day (Gen. 8:22). Now if the measure of the day includes the night in it, why mention night? It is also incorrect from the point of view of the science of linguistics for a noun to refer to two things which are the opposite of each other. The word day is used secondarily in the sense of close or far-off time, as in on the day that I smote all the first-born in the land of Egypt (Num. 3:13); thou art to pass over the Jordan this day (Deut. 9:1); and cast them into another land, as it is this day (Deut. 29:27); And it shall come to pass in that day (Is. 7:21). There are many other similar instances. Now let us leave all these things aside and seek, as I have said, only after the day of the Torah, for our years are not established according to the movement of the sun and moon but rather according to what the Bet Din decrees. Now we find that Scripture states, Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread (Ex. 12:15). Scripture then goes on to explain that this number begins on the evening of the fourteenth of the first month (Ex. 12:18). Scripture also states, from even unto even, shall ye keep your sabbath (Lev. 23:32). Furthermore, a man who has a seminal emission during the night or day, for it is so written, viz., that which chanceth him by night (Deut. 23:11), does not become “clean” until sunset, which is the end of the first day. Now if it were so, namely, that the first day ends on the morning of the next day, then it is only fit for the one who experienced an emission to immerse himself in the morning. For if we say that the day and the night which follows it make up one day then the one who experienced an emission will be “unclean” for half a day and clean for half a day. And one who experienced an emission at the beginning of the night will be unclean for half of a day that passed and also for half of the coming day. This is the opinion of those who err. I have already explained to you the meaning of and there was evening and there was morning (Gen. 1:5) in its place.

AND MOSES SAID. Moses now explained to them what they should do with the additional manna which was laid up, and he revealed to them its secret, that they would not find it this day because it did not come down.
SIX DAYS SHALL YE GATHER IT. It shall always be as it is now for as long as you are in the wilderness; that is, ye shall gather it for six days but on the seventh no manna shall come down.
[IN IT THERE SHALL BE NONE.] The word bo (in it) is added for additional clarification. It is similar to but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it (Gen. 2:17).
AND IT CAME TO PASS ON THE SEVENTH DAY. Of the manna’s appearance.
THAT THERE WENT OUT…TO GATHER. To see whether Moses’ words would stand up.
AND THE LORD SAID UNTO MOSES. Moses was Israel’s representative. The meaning of our verse is: the Lord said unto Moses, tell the following to the Israelites.
[MY COMMANDMENTS.] This was said in reference to the people who left some of the manna over until the morning.

[MY LAWS.] For God taught them the reason for the Sabbath. They therefore gathered twice as much bread on the sixth day. There is a reason why Scripture employs the plural, namely, My commandments and My laws . All the commandments and laws are, beyond any doubt, to be taken literally. However, they have secret meanings pertaining to the soul that only the enlightened can understand. Thus every commandment has two meanings.

SEE. Its meaning is: see the wonder that the Lord will perform for you so that it shall become clear to you that God commanded you to rest as He rested when He made all things in the beginning. God is therefore permitting twice as much manna to come down today as normally comes down every day.
ABIDE YE EVERY MAN IN HIS PLACE. In one’s tent.
[LET NO MAN GO OUT OF HIS PLACE.] It meaning is: let no man go out of his place on the seventh day to gather manna as the men who went out to gather did.
SO THE PEOPLE RESTED. Scripture tells us that from that day on, no man went out on the Sabbath to gather.
AND THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL CALLED THE NAME THEREOF MANNA. Behold, Scripture previously noted the miracles associated with the manna. It now turns to relate its praises.

[AND IT WAS LIKE CORIANDER SEED, WHITE.] Some say that gad (coriander) refers to kosbarta, in Arabic, kusbar. Others say that it means mustard. However, I do not know, as it is not found in any other context save in reference to the manna. The same is the case with the word tzappichat (wafers), which Saadiah Gaon says means an unleavened wafer. Now when the manna was eaten as it was when it came down, it had the taste of a wafer made with honey. However, when cooked it had the taste of a cake baked in oil (Num. 11:8). Scripture mentions these two delicacies.

AND MOSES SAID. This chapter should have followed the account of the construction of the Tabernacle. It was placed here to relate the miracle of the manna lasting for generations. Now Moses told this to Israel. He therefore said, wherewith I fed you .
A JAR. A clay or copper utensil. The word is not found elsewhere.
[BEFORE THE LORD.] Its meaning is, before the divine glory which is upon the cherubim.

AS THE LORD COMMANDED MOSES. Scripture here explains that before the Lord means: before the Testimony, the reference being to the ark. The ark is referred to as the Ark of the Testimony because of the tablets of the covenant that were in it.

AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. This miracle was greater than all the other miracles that were done via Moses, for many miracles were connected with the manna. These miracles, unlike all other wonders, lasted for forty years.

[UNTIL THEY CAME TO A LAND INHABITED.] Scripture says this for they were in the wilderness, in a land that no man passed through (Jer. 2:6). Now once Israel crossed the Jordan they ate the grain that they found there. The reason Scripture found it necessary to say, they did eat the manna, until they came unto the borders of the land of Canaan is that the manna accompanied them until they came to Gilgal, which lies on the border of the land of Canaan. The manna then ceased to fall, for now they had new grain.
NOW AN OMER IS THE TENTH PART OF AN EPHAH. Scripture mentions this measurement because one omer per person was sufficient for satiation.
JOURNEYED. Scripture is being brief in saying by their stages. For from the wilderness of Sin Israel journeyed to Dophkah; from there to Alush, and from Alush they went to Rephidim.
[ACCORDING TO THE COMMANDMENT OF THE LORD.] Its meaning is, as I have already noted, via the hand of Moses.

WHEREFORE THE PEOPLE STROVE. Scripture mentions the people, not all of the people as it does with regard to the manna, for there were two parties. One had no water to drink. This is the group that strove with Moses. The second group had water which they brought from Alush. This group, as Scripture goes on to say, wanted to test God and see if He would provide water.

GIVE US WATER. They spoke to Moses and Aaron. There was no need to mention Aaron, for I have already explained that Moses spoke to Israel only through Aaron. [WHY STRIVE YE WITH ME?] Moses answered them, Why strive ye with me? Let us all cry out unto the Lord. He said, wherefore do ye try the Lord ? to those who wanted to test God.
AND THE PEOPLE THIRSTED. When the thirst overpowered them they raged against Moses and accused him of doing them evil in bringing them out of Egypt.
AND THE PEOPLE CRIED…THEY ARE ALMOST READY TO STONE ME. Scripture speaks metaphorically. Its meaning is: they have striven with me and they rage against me. If they had the power they would stone me.
AND THE LORD SAID. Some say that because Moses said, they are almost ready to stone me, God told him, Pass on before the people who strive with you and inform them that you will now give them water.
AND TAKE WITH THEE OF THE ELDERS OF ISRAEL; AND THY ROD, WHEREWITH THOU SMOTEST THE RIVER. By command.
BEHOLD, I WILL STAND BEFORE THEE THERE UPON THE ROCK IN HOREB. Its meaning is, you will find Me there, the idea being you will encounter My strength and power on Horeb.
AND THOU SHALT STRIKE THE ROCK. Which contains no water.
[AND MOSES DID SO.] Scripture is being brief, for it does not mention, and the congregation drank, and their cattle (Num. 20:11).
CALLED. Moses or someone.

MASSAH AND MERIBAH. Because of the two reasons noted. It is the style of the Hebrew language to begin its comments with the second of two items when two particulars are listed, as the second item is at hand. Compare, And I gave unto Isaac Jacob and Esau (Josh. 24:4), which is followed by and I gave unto Esau ( Ibid .). Scripture similarly first mentions Massah and then Meribah and turns to explain that the name of the place was called Meribah because of the striving of the children of Israel with Moses. It then explains that the place was called Massah because they tried the Lord. Now “trial” refers to Israel’s asking, Is the Lord among us to provide for all of our needs? This second party angered God more than the first. Scripture therefore says, Ye shall not try the Lord your God, as ye tried Him in Massah (Deut. 6:16).
THEN CAME AMALEK. The reference is to the nation of Amalek, which dwelleth in the land of the South (Num. 13:29).

AND MOSES SAID UNTO JOSHUA. Joshua was the grandson of Prince Elishama ben Ammihud, the possessor of the banner of the tribe of Ephraim. Scripture refers to him here as Joshua, which is the name by which Moses called him in the account of the spies.
CHOOSE US OUT. It is Hebrew style to speak in this manner. Compare, choose thee (II Sam. 24:12); Tarry ye here for us (Ex. 24:14).
MEN. Renowned, powerful men and men of war, as in all of them men (Num. 13:3).
AND GO OUT, FIGHT WITH AMALEK. Go out from the camp of Israel to fight against Amalek.
I WILL STAND ON TOP OF THE HILL. Horeb, which is the same as Mount Sinai.
WITH THE ROD OF GOD IN MY HAND. With which I will lift my hand to pray.
SO JOSHUA DID. Aaron and Hur are mentioned because of the need to explain (they) stayed up his hands (v. 12).

AND IT CAME TO PASS. Some say that Moses held his hand up in a manner similar to one holding up a banner in war. However, if this was the case then Aaron or Hur would have lifted the rod up or they would have placed it on a high place on the mountain so that the people would see it standing. The correct interpretation is the one offered by the ancient sages.

BUT MOSES’ HANDS WERE HEAVY. We know that a human being does not have the strength to hold his hands up for an entire day. One cannot even hold them up for a few hours, certainly not until the going down of the sun . Now Scripture notes that Moses’ hands were heavier than the hands of other old people. Moses thus could not continually hold his hands up.
[AND PUT IT.] Its meaning is, they strengthened his place because he was not able to stand up.

AND AARON AND HUR. Stood. Scripture employs the masculine kevedim (heavy) and similarly reads, mi-zeh echad u-mi-zeh echad (the one on the one side, and the other on the other side). Ve-hinneh yad sheluchah elai, ve-hinneh vo megillat sefer (behold, a hand was put forth unto me; and, lo, a roll of a book was therein) is similar (Ezek. 2:9).
AND HIS HANDS WERE STEADY. Each one of his hands. The phrase is grammatically similar to Its branches run over the wall (Gen. 49:22) and But the righteous are secure as a young lion (Prov. 28:1).

STEADY. Emunah (steady) is a noun meaning something lasting and permanent. Others say that emunah comes from the same root as the word omen (brought up) in And he brought up Hadassah (Esth. 2:7). Aaron and Hur were like nursemaids who lifted up his hands.

AND JOSHUA DISCOMFITED AMALEK. There is no difference between va-yachalosh (discomfited or weakened) and va-yechelash (weakened) (Job 14:10). Likewise, the word yitrof (tear) (Ps. 7:3) means the same as yitraf (tears) (Gen. 49:27). The same is the case with the words tiddor (voweth) in voweth a vow (Num. 30:4) and va-yiddar (vowed), which is vocalized with a pattach in and Jacob vowed a vow (Gen. 28:20). However, this root, like the word shav (returned), is sometimes transitive and sometimes intransitive. Or, va-yechelash (weakened) in a man (gever) dieth, and is weakened (Job 14:10) means he was already weakened, like the word va-yivash (and rotted) in and it bred worms, and rotted (Ex. 16:20). Scripture therefore employs the term gever (man), which indicates a mighty man.

WRITE THIS FOR A MEMORIAL IN THE BOOK. This chapter was said in the fortieth year. The fact that Scripture reads ba-sefer (in the book) with a pattach beneath the bet is proof of the aforementioned. For ba-sefer refers to the well-known book, that is, the book of the Torah. It is also possible that they had another book known as The Book of the Wars of the Lord which was lost to us, as were the Sefer Ha-Yashar and the Midrash of Iddo and the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel and the works of Solomon.
[IN THE EARS OF JOSHUA.] For God knew that Joshua was destined to wage war with the kings of Canaan.

[FOR I WILL UTTERLY BLOT OUT THE REMEMBRANCE OF AMALEK.] Because Amalek angered God. For the chiefs of Edom and similarly those of Moab and of Philistia feared and trembled before God because of the signs which the Lord displayed in Egypt and at the sea. Now this very Amalek heard of the might that God displayed on behalf of His people Israel. Behold, he came from a distant place to wage war against Israel. He did not fear God. Indeed, Scripture explicitly states, and he (Amalek) feared not God (Deut. 25:18). Some say that Amalek was the name of a king. They say this because Scripture reads, Amalek and his people. On the other hand, it is possible that another nation joined Amalek.
AND MOSES BUILT AN ALTAR. On Horeb. The word mizbe’ach (altar) is to be read as if written twice. Our verse is to be read as if written, mizbach Adonai (the altar of the Lord).

THE HAND UPON THE THRONE OF THE LORD. It is as if God put His hand upon His throne. This was the taking of an oath. It is similar to For I lift up My hand to heaven (Deut. 32:40). Rabbi Joshua says that its meaning is that the first one to sit upon the throne of Israel, the reference being to Saul, will have a mighty hand. We similarly find it said concerning Solomon: Then Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord (I Chron. 29:23).
